content: 1. The use of elagolix at a dose of 200 mg twice daily in combination with strong CYP3A inhibitors for more than one month is not recommended. This is because elagolix can decrease the levels of certain drugs, such as idelalisib, by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is advised. 2. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate inducer of CYP3A4. When co-administered with CYP3A substrates, their levels should be monitored closely, and dose adjustments may be necessary. 3. Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered, as idelalisib is a strong CYP3A inhibitor. Co-administration with sensitive CYP3A substrates should be avoided or closely monitored. 4. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of ifosfamide by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Additionally, elagolix decreases ifosfamide levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. 5. Iloperidone increases norethindrone acetate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor, which may increase plasma levels of drugs metabolized by CYP3A4. 6. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of imatinib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. However, it also decreases imatinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 7. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of imipramine by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Caution is advised when using sensitive CYP2C19 substrates. 8. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Conversely, indinavir increases elagolix levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. 9. Elagolix decreases the levels of isavuconazonium sulfate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is required. 10. Isoniazid increases elagolix levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. The use of elagolix 200 mg twice daily with strong CYP3A inhibitors for more than one month is not recommended. If co-administered, the elagolix dose should be limited to 150 mg once daily, and the duration of CYP3A inhibitor use should not exceed six months. 11. Elagolix decreases the levels of isosorbide dinitrate and isosorbide mononitrate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are required. 12. Elagolix decreases the levels of isradipine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. 13. Istradefylline increases norethindrone acetate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is required. Istradefylline at 40 mg/day increased the peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates in clinical trials, but this effect was not observed at 20 mg/day. 14. Elagolix decreases istradefylline levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 15. Itraconazole increases elagolix levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. The use of elagolix 200 mg twice daily with strong CYP3A inhibitors for more than one month is not recommended. 16. Elagolix decreases the levels of ivabradine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are required. 17. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of ivermectin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 18. Ivosidenib decreases elagolix levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, elagolix decreases ivosidenib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 19. Ivosidenib decreases norethindrone acetate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. Co-administration of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates with ivosidenib should be avoided or replaced with alternative therapies. If unavoidable, patients should be monitored for loss of therapeutic effects. 20. Elagolix decreases ixabepilone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are required. 21. Elagolix decreases ixazomib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. 22. Elagolix decreases ketamine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 23. Ketoconazole increases elagolix levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. The use of elagolix 200 mg twice daily with strong CYP3A inhibitors for more than one month is not recommended. 24. Elagolix decreases lacosamide levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are required. 25. Elagolix increases lansoprazole levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. Additionally, elagolix decreases lansoprazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. 26. Elagolix increases lapatinib levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. However, it decreases lapatinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 27. Elagolix decreases larotrectinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are required. Conversely, larotrectinib increases elagolix levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, though the clinical significance is unknown. 28. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 29. Elagolix decreases lefamulin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. Co-administration of lefamulin with strong or moderate CYP3A inducers should be avoided unless the benefits outweigh the risks. 30. Elagolix decreases lemborexant levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. 31. Lenacapavir increases elagolix levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. Conversely, elagolix decreases lenacapavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with moderate CYP3A4 inducers should be avoided. 32. Elagolix decreases leniolisib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, leniolisib increases elagolix levels by inhibiting OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 transporters. Alternative drugs should be considered. 33. Lenvatinib increases elagolix levels through other mechanisms. Co-administration is contraindicated. Additionally, elagolix increases lenvatinib levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 34. Elagolix decreases levamlodipine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is required. 35.
